description:
KYNEX is a technology team from Huánuco, Peru, passionate about software development, AI, and innovation.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our goal is to create an interactive educational simulator where students manage lunar and Martian bases, balance resources, overcome environmental challenges, and make critical decisions.

We aim to make space exploration fun, educational, and accessible through technology.
summary:
# KYNEX: Interactive Space Exploration and Survival Trainer

KYNEX is an educational 3D simulation platform that transforms NASA scientific data into interactive experiences to help students understand the challenges of human exploration and survival on the Moon and Mars.

**KYNEX Lunar Lab** recreates a region near Shackleton Crater at the lunar south pole using real topographic data from NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA). Students can explore the terrain, investigate its features, and learn about essential lunar habitat systems, including energy management, life support, and radiation protection.

**KYNEX Mars Frontier** provides an interactive environment inspired by Arcadia Planitia, where students can explore using a rover, investigate geological samples, and study the challenges of establishing a human settlement. Its design draws on scientific research into water resources, environmental conditions, and long-duration mission planning.

By combining virtual exploration, scientific data, and engineering simulations, KYNEX promotes hands-on learning, critical thinking, problem-solving, and interest in space science and technology.
details:
KYNEX — Interactive Moon and Mars Mission Trainer

Project Overview

KYNEX is an interactive 3D educational platform designed to help students explore the challenges of human survival and scientific exploration on the Moon and Mars.

Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our project responds to the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge by transforming space science into immersive, interactive training experiences.

Instead of only reading about space exploration, students can become virtual astronauts, explore extraterrestrial environments, operate scientific equipment, investigate geological samples, and make decisions related to mission safety and resource management.

Our goal is to make space science engaging, accessible, and understandable through exploration and practical problem-solving.

Two Planetary Training Environments

KYNEX Lunar Lab — Moon

Our lunar environment focuses on the challenges of living and surviving on the Moon.

It uses topographic data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) to represent a region near Shackleton Crater at the lunar south pole.

Students can explore the lunar surface, experience simulated lunar gravity, and interact with a fictional lunar research station.

Our central survival scenario is "Survive Your First 24 Hours on the Moon."

This experience focuses on the relationships among electrical power, life-support systems, atmospheric conditions, operational safety, and resource management.

The project also includes educational research concepts involving lunar materials and their potential applications in oxygen production, energy infrastructure, and radiation shielding.

KYNEX Mars Frontier — Mars

Our Mars environment provides a separate interactive exploration experience focused on Arcadia Planitia.

Students explore a simulated Martian landscape, locate a scientific habitat, operate a rover, collect geological samples, and investigate possible resources.

The environment includes an interactive rover with battery monitoring, a sample collection and analysis system, scientific records, a mission interface, and simulated dust-storm events.

A NASA Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) map provides regional topographic context, while the local 3D terrain is a procedural representation rather than a direct reconstruction of measured elevations.

Students can observe how environmental conditions affect exploration, mobility, equipment, and mission safety.

Scientific Foundation

KYNEX combines scientific information with clearly identified educational simulation models.

The Moon environment uses NASA LOLA-derived terrain data, while the Mars environment incorporates NASA MOLA cartographic information.

Our research also draws on scientific knowledge related to planetary environments, geology, life-support systems, solar energy, radiation protection, and space exploration.

A fundamental design principle is distinguishing measured scientific information from derived values, simplified simulations, and fictional training scenarios.

This helps students understand not only scientific facts but also how scientific evidence and models differ.

Technologies Used

Our development tools include:

  • Three.js for interactive 3D rendering.
  • JavaScript for simulation mechanics, movement, and interactions.
  • Vue 3 for the lunar application's user interface.
  • Vite for the lunar application's development and build workflow.
  • HTML and CSS for the Mars Frontier interface.
  • Blender for 3D asset creation and preparation.
  • NASA scientific datasets and planetary mapping resources.

The platform is designed around browser-based access, allowing students to explore the simulations without installing a traditional desktop game.

Creativity and Innovation

KYNEX combines elements of survival games, scientific visualization, virtual exploration, and interactive learning.

The Moon scenario focuses on the challenge of keeping a lunar station operational.

The Mars scenario emphasizes planetary exploration, rover operations, sample analysis, and environmental hazards.

Rather than relying exclusively on traditional lessons or quizzes, KYNEX encourages students to learn through actions, investigation, experimentation, and the consequences of their decisions.

By including both lunar and Martian environments, the project also introduces students to the differences between planetary exploration challenges.

Benefits and Expected Impact

KYNEX aims to encourage interest in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM), especially among students who may not have access to specialized laboratories or space science learning resources.

The project seeks to develop scientific curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and awareness of the challenges involved in human space exploration.

It also demonstrates how NASA's openly available scientific information can support accessible and engaging educational experiences.

Conclusion

KYNEX brings planetary exploration closer to students through interactive simulations of the Moon and Mars.

Our vision is to help young learners understand how astronauts explore unfamiliar environments, investigate scientific evidence, manage resources, and respond to mission challenges.

KYNEX — Explore, experiment, and learn how to survive beyond Earth.
